    Gaussian Process Prediction (with Optional Quadratic Mean)

    predict_gp.Rd

    Compute the posterior mean, covariance, and a single simulation draw from a Gaussian Process (GP) posterior at new input locations. Supports both zero-mean GP and a linear-plus-quadratic mean model.

    predict_gp(data, x_pred, noise_var = 1e-06, choice_cov, quad = FALSE)

    Arguments

    data

    A list with elements:

    • x: numeric vector or matrix of observed inputs (rows = observations).

    • y: numeric vector of observed responses.

    x_pred

    Numeric vector or matrix of input locations at which to predict. Must have the same number of columns as data$x if data$x is a matrix.

    noise_var

    Positive numeric scalar. Observation noise variance to add on the diagonal of the training covariance matrix.

    choice_cov

    A covariance-generating function, such as one returned by cov_generator, that accepts two inputs (x1, x2) and returns their covariance matrix.

    quad

    Logical; if FALSE (default), use a zero-mean GP model. If TRUE, fit a linear-plus-quadratic mean model \(\beta_0 + x^\top \beta_1 + (x \otimes x)^\top \beta_2\) alongside the GP.

    Value

    A list with components:

    x

    The prediction inputs x_pred.

    mean

    Numeric vector of posterior mean values at x_pred.

    var

    Posterior covariance matrix among x_pred.

    sim

    A single draw from the multivariate normal with mean mean and covariance var.

    Details

    For the zero-mean case (quad = FALSE), the function:

    • Constructs \(K_{oo}, K_{op}, K_{pp}\) via choice_cov.

    • Adds noise_var to the diagonal of \(K_{oo}\) and computes its Cholesky factor L.

    • Computes the conditional mean \(K_{op} L^{-T} L^{-1} y\) and covariance \(K_{pp} - K_{op} L^{-T} L^{-1} K_{op}^T\).

    If quad = TRUE, a design matrix with intercept, linear, and unique quadratic terms is built for both observed and prediction inputs, and coefficients \(\beta\) are estimated via generalized least squares. The posterior mean and covariance combine both the mean model and GP residuals.

    Examples

    # Zero-mean GP with SE kernel
cov_fn <- cov_generator(length_scale = 1, signal_var = 1, nu = Inf)
data <- list(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10),
             y = sin(pi * seq(0, 1, length.out = 10)))
preds <- predict_gp(data, x_pred = seq(0, 1, length.out = 50),
                    noise_var = 1e-4, choice_cov = cov_fn)
plot(preds$x, preds$mean, type = "l")


# GP with quadratic mean
preds_quad <- predict_gp(data, x_pred = seq(0, 1, length.out = 50),
                         noise_var = 1e-4, choice_cov = cov_fn,
                         quad = TRUE)
